key_insight: Lower prediction error does not necessarily mean better physical fidelity: models can score well on flow fields while still misrepresenting physically important fluctuation energy.
engineering_relevance: For CFD surrogates and Sim2Real flow models, engineers should evaluate both standard benchmark errors and physics-based diagnostics such as fluctuation energy to avoid misleading model selection.
method: Compared paired CFD simulations and experimental PIV data for flow around a NACA4418 airfoil.
Applied a mean-preserving input intervention that removed velocity fluctuations from selected regions of observed flow histories.
Tested four neural operators with input and output perturbation stress tests to compare prediction sensitivity and physical-statistic errors.
evidence_signal: Across four neural operators, removing fluctuations from the most energetic 10% of valid observed cells changed forecasts more than equal-area random removal, and one CNO showed lower velocity-field error but much higher two-component fluctuation-energy error.
watch_item: The fluctuation-removal masks were not matched for removed energy, so the comparison measures sensitivity rather than proving physical importance or counterfactual correctness.
paper_title: Do Better Scores Mean Better Physics? Physics-Grounded Explanations for Sim2Real Neural Operators
